papers.title: Courtship Behavior and Induced Spawning Dynamics of the Freshwater Shark, Wallago attu, in Captivity: Implications for Silurid Reproductive Strategies.
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.abstract: The vulnerable catfish Wallago attu, a commercially important freshwater species in Southeast Asia, faces population decline due to habitat degradation and overfishing. This study is the first to document the courtship behavior and induced spawning of W. attu under captive conditions in circular spawning tanks. The hormonal induction was achieved using a combination of salmon gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue and domperidone (0.5 mL kg-1 for females; 0.2 mL kg-1 for males). Males exhibited dominant courtship behavior, characterized by aggressive chasing and U-shaped body wrapping around the female's abdomen for 5.15 ± 0.17 s, leading to synchronized gamete release. The latency period prior to the onset of spawning occurred within a time frame of 9-10 h following hormonal administration. The findings indicate that the removal of brooders following egg release resulted in a significantly higher rate of fertilization and hatching, with a percentage of 88.12 ± 0.26%, as compared to 67.78 ± 1.78% in tanks that contained brooders This observation suggests the presence of egg predation. Plastic strings functioned as effective artificial substrates, enhancing fertilization (86.42 ± 1.18%) and hatching (89.28 ± 0.80%) in comparison to aquatic weeds. The findings presented herein provide a foundation of information upon which the establishment of efficient captive breeding and hatchery protocols for W. attu can be based. Such protocols will in turn support the conservation of the species and the sustainable development of aquaculture.

papers.title: Optic Nerve Sheath Meningiomas: A Narrative Review of Clinical Features, Imaging Advances, and Current Management.
papers.abstract: Optic nerve sheath meningioma (ONSM) is a rare orbital tumor that can pose a significant threat to visual function due to its close relationship with the optic nerve and surrounding vascular structures. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential to preserve vision and guide individualized management. The objective of this narrative review is to provide a comprehensive overview of the current evidence on the clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, imaging characteristics, and management of ONSM, with a particular focus on recent advances in imaging techniques and their implications for clinical decision-making. This review synthesizes current knowledge on clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and evolving treatment strategies for ONSM, with particular emphasis on advanced imaging modalities. Magnetic resonance imaging remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, yet functional imaging, especially somatostatin receptor--based techniques such as 68GaDOTATATE PET/CT have shown potential as a useful adjunct in the diagnostic evaluation of ONSM, especially for assessing tumor characteristics, extent, and treatment planning in selected cases. We discuss the emerging role of DOTATATE imaging in differentiating ONSM from other optic nerve and orbital pathologies, as well as its potential application in monitoring therapeutic response. We also highlight contemporary management approaches, including fractionated radiotherapy and the selective role of surgical intervention, underscoring the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making in optimizing visual outcomes. Emerging molecular insights from meningioma research may inform future therapeutic strategies for ONSM; however, clinical evidence specific to ONSM remains limited.

papers.title: Effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength and functional outcomes in individuals with subacromial pain syndrome: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Subacromial pain syndrome (SAPS) is one of the most common causes of shoulder pain and is frequently associated with rotator cuff dysfunction. Recent evidence suggests a close relationship between hand grip strength and rotator cuff muscle function, indicating that grip-strengthening exercises may enhance shoulder rehabilitation outcomes. To investigate the effects of grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise on shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes in individuals with SAPS. METHODS: Thirty-six individuals with SAPS were randomly assigned to an experimental group (scapular stabilization exercise combined with grip strengthening; n = 18) or a control group (scapular stabilization exercise alone; n = 18). Both groups participated in exercise sessions 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes using the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index were assessed before and after the intervention. RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvements in shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and Shoulder Pain and Disability Index scores (P < .001). Significant Time × Group interaction effects were observed for all outcome measures (P < .001), indicating greater improvements in the experimental group. CONCLUSIONS: Grip strengthening combined with scapular stabilization exercise may provide additional benefits for improving shoulder muscle strength, grip strength, and functional outcomes in individuals with SAPS.

papers.title: The Great EFT Schism: Testing Johnson's and Greenberg's Alternative Models of What Drives Couple Satisfaction.
papers.abstract: Emotion-focused therapy for couples (EFT-C) is organized around two theoretical accounts: Johnson's (2019) attachment-based model, which treats attachment as the primary motivational system in romantic relationships, and the Greenberg-Goldman (2008) multi-motivational model, which adds regard and attraction to attachment as three co-equal systems. Their relative explanatory power has not been directly compared. The present study tested whether the multi-motivational model explains more variance in relationship satisfaction than an attachment-only model in a non-clinical community sample. A nationally quota-representative sample of 1090 individuals nested in 545 couples completed measures of relationship satisfaction (CSI-16), attachment behaviors (BARE), interpersonal attraction (IAS), and level of regard (BLRI). Hierarchical regression and relative weights analysis compared model performance, with generalized estimating equations and cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals accounting for non-independence within couples. The attachment-only model explained 47% of variance; adding attraction and regard increased this to 70.5% (ΔR2 = 0.235, Cohen's f2 = 0.80). Contrary to expectations, regard emerged as the dominant predictor (41.3% of explained variance), followed by attraction (29.8%) and attachment (29.0%). Perceived partner regard uniquely predicted satisfaction (p < 0.001), whereas self-reported regard for partner did not (p = 0.663). Conclusions about clinical mechanisms cannot be drawn from this cross-sectional, non-clinical design. Nonetheless, the findings are inconsistent with the strong form of the attachment primacy hypothesis and consistent with the Greenberg-Goldman multi-motivational account. Comprehensive assessment of distressed couples may benefit from attending to regard and attraction alongside attachment.

papers.title: Emotion regulation in couples' conflict memories: A dyadic examination of relationship quality.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Although conflicts in a romantic relationship are known to impact its quality, how individuals keep emotionally regulating the memory of these conflicts could also be associated with both partners' relationship quality. The present study investigated whether the emotion regulation strategies used during recall of a couple conflict memory were differentially associated with the perceived relationship quality of both partners. A total of 218 participants (109 couples) reported their general emotion regulation strategies and perception of relationship quality. Each participant subsequently described a specific conflict memory within the relationship, and judges independently rated the intensity of the reported conflict. Participants also reported the emotion regulation strategy they still used when recalling the conflict. Emotion regulation strategies involved either actively engaging with negative emotions, accepting them, and deriving meaning from the experience (i.e., integrative emotion regulation) or difficulty in adequately managing the negative emotions when recalling the conflict, leading to an overwhelming experience (i.e., dysregulation). A multilevel model revealed that integrative regulation during retrieval of conflict memories was positively associated with self-perceived relationship quality. In contrast, dysregulation during retrieval of conflict memories was negatively associated with both partners' perceived relationship quality. Importantly, these results remained significant even after accounting for how people generally regulate their emotions in daily life, as well as the intensity of the conflict. Our findings suggest that the emotion regulation used when retrieving a conflict memory may modulate each partner's perceived relationship quality. papers.title: Power predicts declines in oppositional behavior over time in newlyweds.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: In romantic relationships, people's goals will inevitably diverge from their partner's at times. When these conflicts arise, people often oppose their partner, such as by blaming their partner or making passive-aggressive comments. Given that opposition aims to influence a partner's attitudes or behavior, oppositional behavior is likely tied to people's sense of power in the relationship. However, past theory and research provide competing hypotheses about the nature of this association; specifically, there are reasons to expect that power could either increase or decrease opposition and/or opposition could either increase or decrease power. Further, previous research addressing this association has been cross-sectional, thus preventing conclusions about the temporal association between power and opposition in romantic relationships. A 2-year longitudinal study of newlyweds indicated that a person's feelings of power predicted declines in both their own and their partners' opposition, but a person's opposition did not predict changes in either their own or their partner's feelings of power. These findings lend support to theories of power in romantic relationships that posit that power decreases oppositional behavior. Moreover, they suggest that addressing either or both partners' feelings of power may be a fruitful avenue for reducing romantic couples' oppositional behavior during conflicts. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Anchoring Anatolian tree-rings and Mesopotamian chronology with single-year radiocarbon patterns and ice-core evidence.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: The historical chronology of Mesopotamia offers a key chronological bridge to connect the Near East and eastern Mediterranean during the second millennium BCE. It is unusually rich in written records, including king lists, administrative documents, royal inscriptions, and astronomical observations. The latter offer a number of alternate possible absolute anchor points, resulting in competing high, middle, low, and ultra-low temporal frameworks. Establishing which of these is correct has consequences far beyond Mesopotamia. Tree-ring sequences from preserved timbers at archaeological sites in Anatolia, linked directly to Mesopotamia via the Old Assyrian trade network, could provide the answer. However, attempts have been limited by the lack of calendar secured dendrochronological dating for these timbers. Here we develop transferable methodologies in single-year radiocarbon analysis, utilizing patterns of 14C preserved in single tree rings from Anatolian timbers to anchor their combined chronology 2072 BCE-744 BCE. This provides a calendrically-secured reference chronology for wood samples from Anatolian sites during this period as well as an annually resolved paleoclimatic record. Tree-ring dates are combined with archaeological and high-resolution ice-core evidence to evaluate the competing chronological frameworks for Mesopotamia between 2000 and 1500 BCE. Remaining dating uncertainties are constrained in strong support of the middle-low chronology.

papers.title: More Than Just a Happy Ending? The Role of Orgasm Consistency for Sexual Satisfaction, Relationship Satisfaction, and Emotional Intimacy in Mixed-Gender Romantic Relationships.
papers.abstract: Orgasm consistency is defined as the frequency with which individuals achieve orgasm during sexual encounters with a partner, while orgasm discrepancy is defined as the difference between the orgasm consistency of two partners. Orgasm consistency has been linked to sexual and relational well-being, yet little is known about how orgasm discrepancy in partners were associated with these factors. This study examined whether orgasm consistency as well as orgasm discrepancy in couples was associated with sexual satisfaction, relationship satisfaction, and emotional intimacy. Data from 327 couples were analyzed using Dyadic Response Surface Analysis. Higher orgasm consistency was associated with greater sexual satisfaction and relationship satisfaction, particularly among men, and with higher emotional intimacy among women. Contrary to expectations, couples with higher levels of orgasm discrepancy reported higher relationship satisfaction than couples with lower levels of orgasm discrepancy. Findings suggest that higher orgasm consistency may serve as a sexual reward, while orgasm discrepancy may not be perceived as a cost. Gendered sexual scripts likely shape these patterns. Overall, models explained limited variance, indicating that other factors beyond orgasm consistency are critical for sexual and relational well-being.

papers.title: Distinct Cross-Lagged Relations of Cognitive Reappraisal and Expressive Suppression With Perceived Social Support Among Chinese Adolescents.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Converging evidence suggests a close relationship between emotion regulation (ER) and perceived social support (PSS) among adolescents. Yet, little is currently known about their longitudinal cross-lagged associations within the Chinese cultural context, as well as the differential effects of different ER strategies. To address these gaps, the present study aimed to examine the cross-lagged associations between PSS and two specific ER strategies-cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression-in Chinese adolescents. METHODS: A total of 316 adolescents from Zhoukou, China (45.9% female; Mage = 16.42, SD = 0.61, aged 14-18 years) participated in a three-wave longitudinal study, with data collected at 6-month intervals during senior high school. To examine hypothesized cross-lagged associations, we employed cross-lagged panel models, a well-established method for analyzing temporal associations (Kenny 1975). RESULTS: Cross-lagged panel model revealed that PSS at Time 1 was positively associated with cognitive reappraisal at Time 2, which in turn was positively related to PSS at Time 3. PSS at Time 2 also showed a positive correlation with cognitive reappraisal at Time 3. In contrast, no significant cross-lagged effects were observed between PSS and expressive suppression over time. CONCLUSIONS: These findings contribute to a more nuanced understanding of the longitudinal cross-lagged associations between PSS and ER in adolescence, highlighting the association between supportive social environments and adolescents' ER strategies.

papers.title: Demographic Reporting and Analysis in Gait Biomechanics of Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the leading causes of disability in the United States. Biomechanics research has expanded knowledge on knee OA presentation, progression, and treatment, with clinical practices evolving based on biomechanical discoveries. In the United States, patients with knee OA are diverse across various demographics, including age, sex, body mass index, race, and ethnicity. Given the close relationship between biomechanics research and clinical practice, it is important that biomechanical studies reflect the diverse clinical population. This scoping review evaluates the hypotheses that demographics in knee OA gait biomechanical studies are underreported and do not represent the clinical population in the United States. Research articles published between 2016 and 2024 were screened, and 58 articles were evaluated. Participant age and sex were reported in 98% of articles, while only 12% and 7% of articles reported race and ethnicity, respectively. Average study participant age and sex were representative of the clinical population. However, only a few articles reported comprehensive race and ethnicity data, so clinical comparison was inconclusive. This scoping review demonstrates the need for more comprehensive demographic reporting in knee OA gait biomechanics studies to enable a widely applicable understanding of the disease and development of optimal treatments.

papers.title: Endodontic-Periodontal Lesions: Biological Basis, Diagnostic Challenges, and Contemporary Management Strategies.
papers.abstract: The dental pulp and periodontium are intimately connected through anatomical structures such as the apical foramen, lateral and accessory canals, and dentinal tubules, creating pathways for the bidirectional spread of infection and inflammation. This close relationship can result in endodontic-periodontal lesions, which often present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to overlapping clinical and radiographic features. This review aims to examine the etiopathogenesis, classification, diagnostic considerations, and contemporary management approaches for endodontic-periodontal lesions. A narrative review of classical and current literature was conducted, focusing on the anatomical and biological interrelationship between pulpal and periodontal tissues, microbial interactions, disease progression, and evidence-based treatment protocols. The reviewed literature indicates that endodontic infections commonly produce secondary periodontal manifestations through the dissemination of microorganisms and their by-products along established anatomical pathways, while advanced periodontal disease may, under certain circumstances, adversely affect pulpal health. Accurate diagnosis requires a comprehensive assessment incorporating pulp vitality testing, periodontal examination, probing patterns, radiographic evaluation, and correlation of clinical findings. Successful treatment outcomes depend on correctly identifying the primary source of infection and implementing an appropriate treatment sequence. In most cases, endodontic therapy should be initiated before periodontal intervention to facilitate healing, permit reassessment of periodontal status, and guide the need for additional periodontal treatment. A thorough understanding of the endodontic-periodontal relationship remains essential for predictable diagnosis, treatment planning, and long-term prognosis. papers.title: Steinernema chainatense n. sp., a new entomopathogenic nematode (Nematoda: Steinernematidae) from Thailand.
papers.abstract: A new entomopathogenic nematode, Steinernema chainatense n. sp., was isolated during sampling in a cassava field in Chai Nat Province, Central Thailand. A combination of morphological, morphometric, and molecular traits places the new species within the longicaudum clade of the glaseri-group. Infective juveniles (IJs) of S. chainatense n. sp. are characterised by a body length of 871 (798-939) μm, a maximum body diameter of 27 (24-30) μm, and a lateral field with eight equally developed ridges at mid-body and a formula of 2, 6, 8, 2. First-generation males are characterised by large, brown spicules, 88 (80-95) μm long, with a well-developed velum. The male genital papillae number 25 in total, comprising 12 pairs and a single midventral papilla. The internal transcribed spacer (ITS) and D2-D3 sequences differ from those of other members of the longicaudum clade by 3.6-10.4% and 1.5-3.5%, respectively. Phylogenetic analysis based on the ITS region of rDNA indicates a close relationship between S. chainatense n. sp. and S. taiwanensis, S. adamsi, S. guangdongense, and S. longicaudum, with S. taiwanensis as its sister taxon. The bacterial symbiont of S. chainatense n. sp. is the recently described Xenorhabdus thailandensis. These morphological and molecular differences support the recognition of S. chainatense n. sp. as a distinct species.

papers.title: Appearance Over Health: A Phenomenological Study of Obese Adolescents With a Family History of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in a Collectivistic Indonesian Context.
papers.journal: Journal of general and family medicine
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), and Indonesia ranks fifth in the prevalence of diabetes worldwide, coupled with the increasing rate of youth obesity. This phenomenological study explored adolescent obesity as a high-risk group within Indonesia's collectivistic cultural context to generate qualitative insights that may inform culturally grounded, family- and peer-supported interventions for T2DM prevention. The study does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific intervention. METHODS: Conducted in Surakarta, Central Java, Indonesia (March 2021-April 2022), the study recruited 11 adolescents, 11 parents, and 9 peers from four primary care clinics using purposive sampling until data saturation. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's method. RESULTS: The majority of adolescents reported being more concerned about their appearance than about their health. The findings also indicated that all groups had limited awareness of T2DM risks. Adolescents perceived intimate relationships as important in shaping healthy lifestyle choices. Peers offered emotional support and encouragement for healthier behaviors, while parents were described as supervising diet and promoting physical exercise. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that health education could potentially address adolescents' appearance-related concerns as an initial entry point to enhance engagement. For Indonesian adolescents to effectively avoid obesity and lower their risk of T2DM, strategies involving peers and parents may be an important consideration; however, these are presented as implications derived from the qualitative findings, rather than as interventions whose effectiveness has been demonstrated. Future research is needed to empirically test such culturally tailored approaches.

papers.title: Mate recognition in orchid bees is mediated by acquired chemical signals.
papers.journal: Behavioral ecology : official journal of the International Society for Behavioral Ecology
papers.abstract: The evolution of prezygotic reproductive barriers plays a central role in speciation and is often mediated by divergence in mating signals. Male orchid bees collect volatile compounds from the environment to concoct species-specific perfumes that function as sexual chemical signals during courtship display. While perfumes are thought to convey species recognition, their direct role in assortative mating remains unresolved. Here, we experimentally tested whether perfume composition facilitates mate recognition between 2 recently diverged and sympatric sister species, Euglossa dilemma and E. viridissima. We collected perfumes from males in sympatric regions of Mexico and experimentally supplemented E. dilemma males with either conspecific (E. dilemma) or heterospecific (E. viridissima) perfumes. We conducted single-choice mating assays and found that the rate of male courtship display did not differ between treatments. However, females of E. dilemma exhibited a strong preference for males with conspecific perfumes. While 77% of males loaded with E. dilemma perfume mated, only 8% of males loaded with E. viridissima perfume mated. Our results support the hypothesis that perfume composition alone can mediate reproductive isolation in orchid bees. These findings highlight the role of environmentally acquired signals as extended phenotypes that can rapidly generate behavioral isolation and contribute to speciation.

papers.title: From Match to Menace: A Systematic Literature Review of Violence Across Online Dating Platforms.
papers.abstract: This systematic literature review explores the prevalence and ways violence is enacted across online dating platforms. Drawing on 35 peer-reviewed publications from 2014 to 2025, the review uses the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension) methodology. A systematic search was conducted across SagePub, PubPsych and ScienceDirect. The review identified 42 distinct forms of violence and categorised these using a dual-axis framework which considered the Delivery method and the Type of harm enacted. Messaging was the most common Delivery method of violence, with 29 of 42 types of violence occurring through this medium. The second most common Delivery method, shown in 26 of 42 forms of violence was the transition of online to offline interactions. This was violence which occurred in-person proceeding the formation of an online acquaintanceship. Sexual violence was the most common Type of harm, shown in 21 of 42 forms of violence. Psychological/emotional harm was the second most common Type of harm shown in 20 of 42 forms of violence. The findings support previous literature indicating that online dating platforms are environments where violence is normalised and inadequately addressed. The review ultimately highlights the need for urgent, systemic intervention by platform developers and policymakers.

papers.title: The sociopolitical dimension of attachment: differences in attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance between East and West Germans.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Attachment is a universal, cross-cultural basic need, which, however, is defined, satisfied and shaped differently in each socio-cultural context. Germany with its history of two divided states and their different sociopolitical environments offers an unique opportunity to study their impact on attachment behavior. METHODS: Attachment behavior was assessed in a representative sample (N = 2,328) using the dimensions of attachment anxiety and attachment avoidance in couple relationships of the Experiences in Close Relationships questionnaire (ECR-RD 12). Differences between East and West Germans were examined in a univariate analysis of variance, differentiated by age cohorts and sex. Socioeconomic variables were included in the model as control variables. RESULTS: Significant East-West differences were found for attachment anxiety (p = .01), but not for attachment avoidance. The analysis differentiated by age cohorts revealed on average a lower level of attachment anxiety for East Germans born between 1921 and 1989 compared to West Germans. These differences were not found for the post-reunification generation (born after 1989), although this comparison included only 28 East German participants and should be interpreted with caution. Gender-related effects were only found in relation with age cohorts. CONCLUSION: Adults who grew up in the former German Democratic Republic (GDR) report lower attachment anxiety than their West German counterparts. Although effect sizes were small, the findings suggest that the sociopolitical environment is a relevant factor for attachment behavior in close relationships, particularly attachment anxiety.

papers.title: Burrow morphology and behavior of Parasesarma eumolpe across contrasting mangrove environments in the Mekong Delta.
papers.abstract: Burrowing behavior is an important component of soft-sediment ecosystems because excavation modifies sediment structure and provides below-ground habitat. In mangrove forests, sesarmid crabs are prominent burrowers, but the extent to which burrow architecture varies among local environments remains incompletely described. We quantified 177 Parasesarma eumolpe burrows from two mangrove sites in the Mekong Delta that differed in salinity, pH, vegetation, and qualitative sediment characteristics. Eight morphotypes were recognized, and burrow depth, total length, mouth diameter, chamber diameter, number of entrances and chambers, and cast weight were recorded. I- and J-shaped burrows were the most frequent morphotypes. The distribution of morphotypes differed between sites (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact p = 0.00074), although the main effect of site was not significant for the continuous morphometric variables evaluated by two-way ANOVA. Burrow length and depth differed among morphotypes, whereas mouth and chamber diameters did not. Field observations documented excavation, entrance maintenance, territorial interactions, food transport, courtship, and the occurrence of juveniles and egg-like particles near or within some complex burrows. Because sediment properties, root structure, crab body size, and reproductive status were not quantified at the individual-burrow level, these observations do not establish causal mechanisms for burrow shape. The results, therefore, demonstrate substantial structural variation in P. eumolpe burrows and identify site-associated differences in morphotype frequencies while providing a conservative basis for hypotheses about environmental and behavioral influences on burrow architecture.

papers.title: Francophone Expert Consensus on Onco-Sexological Care for Prostate Cancer.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although it is well known that prostate cancer treatments have a significant impact on sexuality and intimate relationships, this aspect is not given sufficient consideration in clinical practice. Thus, to date, there is no Francophone guideline on the onco-sexological care for prostate cancer. We therefore decided to proceed with a formalized expert consensus, using the method recommended by the French National Authority for Health. The aim was to provide the French urology and sexual medicine community with practice guidelines applicable to all patients treated for prostate cancer, regardless of the treatment, throughout the care pathway. METHODS: Twenty-five international experts met online for the consensus. A research committee carried out a comprehensive literature review and prepared the 64 statements submitted to the rating group. After one round of scoring, 58 recommendations were validated in July 2025, having achieved a consensus of more than 70% among the experts. RESULTS: The consensus focused on Informing patients and partners, assessing and treating sexual dysfunction and distress, providing lifestyle and psychosocial recommendations, as well as organisational and public health considerations. It is recommended that an oncosexological care pathway include: pre-treatment information, standardised screening based on patient-reported outcomes, early post-treatment assessment with regular reassessments, and access to a multidisciplinary care pathway. CONCLUSIONS: The expert consensus on Onco-Sexological Care for Prostate Cancer led to the development of clinical guidelines based on the available literature and expert opinion. To achieve this, professionals must mobilize all available resources within the community and the cancer care network.

papers.title: Molecular-based phylogeny and ages of divergence of the subfamily Bryocorinae (Insecta: Heteroptera: Miridae).
papers.abstract: TAXON: Bryocorinae (Insecta: Heteroptera: Miridae) is a subfamily comprising approximately 1100 species, predominantly inhabiting tropical and subtropical regions. CONTEXT: The monophyly of the subfamily and its tribes remains doubtful, and previous studies have yielded contradictory results. AIM: In this study, a molecular phylogenetic analysis of Bryocorinae was performed to test the monophyly of the subfamily and its subgrouping and to estimate their divergence times. METHODS: The analysis was based on mitochondrial (COI, 12S rRNA, and 16S rRNA) and nuclear (18S rRNA and 28S rRNA) markers. Maximum-likelihood analysis was performed using RAxML, and Bayesian inference analyses were conducted using MrBayes and BEAST2. The phylogeny was calibrated using BEAST2. KEY RESULTS: The analysis did not confirm the monophyly of Bryocorinae. Bryocorini and Monaloniini are recovered as monophyletic and are therefore both raised to subfamily rank. Dicyphus forms a clade with Felisacini; consequently, Dicyphini are restricted to a single genus. These two tribes are placed in the subfamily Dicyphinae. The other genera previously included in Dicyphini are placed in the subfamily Macrolophinae. Eccritotarsini are restricted to a clade comprising the greatest number of genera, and this group is raised to subfamily rank. Dating analyses showed that three subfamilies, distributed predominantly in tropical and subtropical regions across the different zoogeographical regions including the New World, originated and diversified around the Mesozoic-Cenozoic boundary (Dicyphinae, Eccritotarsinae, and Monaloniinae). Macrolophinae, which successfully colonized the temperate regions of different continents, most probably, originated during the Cenozoic. The morphologically conserved groups, i.e. Bryocorinae and Felisacini, originated and diversified during the Cenozoic. papers.title: The collective role of bending, stretching, and polydispersity in microtubule mechanics and hydrodynamics.
papers.abstract: Microtubules (MTs) organize into various structures by modulating their physico-chemical and electro-mechanical properties. Their size and flexibility are crucial for maintaining the cell's mechanical strength and its ability to respond to external forces. Translational and rotational diffusion enhance MTs' capacity to locate and bind to targets. In addition, cells regulate asymmetric MT length growth and polydispersity to maintain proper cytoskeletal organization in response to functional demands. Therefore, understanding these properties accurately is essential for grasping their critical roles in cellular functions. In this study, we develop a comprehensive framework to characterize the collective effects of hydrodynamic interactions, polydispersity, bending, and stretching on the hydrodynamic and mechanical properties of MT solutions. The approach integrates dynamic light scattering (DLS), a reliable sample preparation protocol, and an optimized scattering theory for polydisperse semiflexible polymers, yielding accurate, reproducible results from autocorrelation functions measured under conditions that simulate the physiological environment. Overall, the approach offers an alternative to conventional post-analysis DLS tools for analyzing experimental autocorrelation data in filamentous systems with variable stiffness and length and under various intracellular conditions, thereby providing a close relationship among the biophysical parameters describing filaments, their surrounding environment, and their influence on the complex and dynamic behavior of these systems.

papers.title: The effect of seismic shooting on the courtship behaviour of cod (Gadus morhua).
papers.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a well-recognized stressor in the marine environment. Seismic airguns, used to locate oil and gas deposits in the seabed, are among the loudest sources of anthropogenic noise in the North Sea. Their low-frequency sounds overlap with the hearing and vocalisations range of many teleost fishes. Cod (Gadus morhua) produce sounds both during courtship and male-male aggression, and seismic surveys may therefore interfere spawning behaviour. In large spawning pens, we exposed spawning groups of wild caught cod to three hours of daily seismic shooting at varying distances to mimic what fish would be exposed to during a real seismic survey. We examined both short-term (minutes before and after individual air gun shots)) and long-term responses (hours to days, before, during and after the full exposure period) on spawning behaviour. Short-term effects included startle responses, reduction in courtship behaviours, and increased activity in female fish, but no significant effect on vocalisation. The only long-term effect was a significant reduction of flaunting behaviour, while all other reproductive behaviours were resumed quickly after exposure. In conclusion, our study shows that seismic shooting, at levels up to ~165 dB re 1μPa2s (similar to levels found about 5-35 km from a conventional survey) may affect cod courtship behaviour at each onset, within a time frame of minutes from the first close by shot, but not over subsequent hours or days.

papers.title: Conserved DNA methylation architectures are associated with transcriptional robustness and regulatory plasticity in the woody perennial tea plant.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is an important mechanism in plant development and environmental adaptation, yet how distinct methylation features contribute to transcriptional stability and regulatory flexibility in long-lived woody plants remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated DNA methylomes, transcriptomes, and chromatin accessibility profiles from two Camellia sinensis varieties to examine the regulatory characteristics and conservation of two specific methylation architectures: gene body methylation (gbM) and DNA methylation valleys (DMVs). We found that gbM genes showed distinctive gene structures, broad and relatively stable expression, and highly conserved methylation states between orthologs. gbM-gbM orthologs also showed evidence of stronger selective constraint in a sequence-length-dependent manner, consistent with a close relationship between gbM and stable transcription of housekeeping genes. In contrast, DMVs were highly hypomethylated regions associated with TE depletion and pronounced TF footprint signals, both of which were closely linked with methylation level, while DMV-associated genes were enriched for developmental and stress-responsive functions. Genome synteny analyses further revealed substantial conservation of DMV patterns and TF footprint profiles between tea varieties, indicating broad conservation of DMV-associated regulatory features across divergent genetic backgrounds. Together, these findings reveal two complementary epigenetic architectures in a woody perennial plant, with gbM preferentially associated with transcriptional robustness and DMVs with regulatory features linked to development and environmental responses.

papers.title: Assessing the Implementation of the Nonprofit Hospital Community Benefit Program: 15 Years Post-Affordable Care Act.
papers.abstract: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. The program has undergone several regulatory changes over the years to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability; the most recent changes were implemented through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA). As the 15-year anniversary of the ACA approaches, this article provides an in-depth review of the literature on how nonprofit hospitals have responded to ACA Section 9007 ("Additional Requirements for Charitable Hospitals"). This review summarizes the state of the evidence on CB activities specific to the ACA provisions as well as other related recent state policies, discusses CB spending, identifies gaps in the CB literature, and proposes a research agenda for the next 10 years to continue to build the evidence base on hospital CB activities. In addition to contributing to academic literature, this review provides a foundation for policymakers and practitioners as they consider additional reforms to the CB program to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability.

papers.title: Immunohistochemical markers for dating cardiac conduction system injury: current knowledge and forensic implications.
papers.abstract: The postmortem timing of myocardial injury remains a major challenge in forensic pathology, particularly when conventional histological methods are insufficient during the early hours after an ischemic insult. We conducted a critical narrative review of immunohistochemical markers for myocardial injury dating, focusing on their biological applicability to the cardiac conduction system (CCS). The search was performed using PubMed and Scopus; no date restriction was applied. Over the past three decades, markers including complement components (C5b-9), cardiac troponins, fibronectin, and connexin 43 have been investigated, with varying degrees of validation, for injury dating in working ventricular myocardium. However, the CCS - comprising the sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, bundle of His, and Purkinje fibers - is a histologically and molecularly distinct tissue that has received remarkably little attention in this context. We highlight fundamental differences in cellular composition, connexin expression profiles, extracellular matrix content, and baseline protein abundance between conduction and ventricular tissue that are likely to significantly alter marker behavior and temporal kinetics. The direct application of ventricular-based immunohistochemical timelines to the CCS lacks empirical support and may lead to forensic misinterpretation. The medico-legal implications are potentially significant, as accurate timing of conduction system injury is relevant to cases of sudden unexplained death, drug-induced arrhythmias, blunt cardiac trauma, and medical negligence litigation. Systematic, tissue-specific validation studies are urgently needed.

papers.title: Who authored Gyrodactylidae? Resolving the authorship of a widely used monogenoidean family-group under article 11.7.2 of the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature.
papers.abstract: Authorship of the nominal family Gyrodactylidae has been inconsistently cited for more than a century, being generally attributed either to van Beneden & Hesse (1863) or to Cobbold (1864). We evaluated the competing attributions under Article 11.7.2 of the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature. This provision allows a pre-1900 family-group name published in non-latinized form to retain its original authorship if it was later latinized and has been generally accepted as valid and as dating from the first publication in vernacular form. Van Beneden & Hesse (1863) originally established the taxon under the French vernacular Gyrodactylidés. Shortly thereafter, Cobbold (1864) published the latinized form Gyrodactylidae. Review of the historical literature demonstrated persistent attribution to van Beneden & Hesse (1863) across a broad range of taxonomic traditions and geographic regions, even while attribution to Cobbold (1864) has also continued. The conditions of Article 11.7.2 are satisfied, and the nominal family of the family-group should be cited as Gyrodactylidae Van Beneden & Hesse, 1863. This clarification resolves a long-standing nomenclatural inconsistency that persists in both the primary literature and major taxonomic databases.

papers.title: Genotypic and phylogenetic characterization of Salmonella Minnesota ST548 strains with potential risk to public health.
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
papers.abstract: Salmonella Minnesota ST548 has emerged as an important serovar in the poultry industry and has been detected in food products. Five nonclonal S. Minnesota isolates from poultry in southeastern Brazil were characterized using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and 263 database sequences were analyzed for virulence genes, antimicrobial resistance genes, and phylogenetic relationships. Among the analyzed sequences, 191 multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains carried antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) conferring resistance to aminoglycosides (aac(6')-Iaa, aph(3')-Ia and aadA1), quinolones (qnrB19), tetracycline (tetA), sulfonamides (sul2), and beta-lactams (blaCMY-2, blaCTX-M-8, blaCTX-M-55 and blaTEM-126). Furthermore, several genes associated with virulence factors were identified, including adherence (faeC, faeE, and fimB), fimbrial adherence determinants (pegA, staA, fimA, and csgD), magnesium uptake (mgtB and mgtC), macrophage inducible genes (mig-14), toxin (cdtB) and secretion system (ssaM, sseE and sseJ). Twenty-five plasmid replicons and 53 distinct prophages were identified in the analyzed sequences. Phylogenetic analysis showed close relationships between nonclonal S. Minnesota poultry isolates from southeastern Brazil and S. Minnesota sequences associated with human outbreaks from other sources and countries. These findings highlight the need for surveillance of this serovar in both public and veterinary health.

papers.title: What modern genomes overlook: Ancient DNA rewrites the phylogeography of European atlantic salmon (Salmo salar).
papers.abstract: Conservation plans for declining species often rely on contemporary genetic/genomic data to infer historical population structure and evolutionary history of the species. However, modern samples alone may not accurately reflect historical genetic variation, especially after severe population declines or intensive management, and need reference baseline data prior to anthropogenic impact. We analyzed whole-genome sequences dating to 18,800-16,700 years ago from Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), that experienced major declines over the past century. Comparing Paleolithic and modern genomes, we found that ancient salmon from the Iberian glacial refugium were genetically closer to present-day northern European populations than to modern Iberian salmon, consistent with southward displacement of northern lineages during glacial periods, postglacial decline of Iberian populations, and contemporary human impacts. We identified ancient SNPs linked to reproduction and age at maturation in modern salmon populations, while high ancient mitochondrial effective population size suggests greater prehistoric female lineage diversity. These genetic discontinuities between ancient and modern Iberian salmon, not evident in modern samples alone, highlight the value of ancient genomics in conservation.

papers.title: Safety and hospital pharmacy implications of extended beyond-use dating for intravenous anticancer and supportive care admixtures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
papers.abstract: IntroductionThe stability of intravenous drug admixtures is essential for ensuring safety, efficacy, and efficient resource utilization in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the physicochemical stability of intravenous anticancer and supportive-care admixtures and examined the influence of drug class, storage temperature, light exposure, container type, and diluent selection.MethodsThe review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261368183). Thirty-three studies were included. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled stability durations, with subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and risk-of-bias assessment across six domains.ResultsThe pooled mean maximum stability duration was 30.7 days (95% CI 20.1-41.3; prediction interval 1.4-60.0 days), with extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 99.7%), limiting generalizability. Monoclonal antibodies generally showed longer stability than cytotoxic agents, particularly under refrigeration. Refrigeration was associated with modestly longer stability, while light exposure appeared to reduce stability, although evidence was limited. Container and diluent effects were variable and drug dependent. Only 12.1% of studies included microbiological assessment, and overall study quality was moderate.ConclusionsIntravenous drug admixtures may remain physicochemically stable beyond manufacturer-defined beyond-use dates under controlled conditions. However, extended beyond-use dating should not be based on physicochemical evidence alone. Drug-specific assessment, sterility assurance, and preferably local validation are required before implementation in hospital pharmacy practice.

papers.title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology.
papers.abstract: The taxonomy and phylogeny of late Middle Pleistocene hominins in East Asia remain highly debated1. Xujiayao, a key representative assemblage with many fossils and a clear stratigraphy dating to around 199-138 thousand years ago, has been extensively studied, but its evolutionary position remains uncertain. Here, to clarify this, we analysed Xujiayao material through both palaeoproteomic analysis and morphological comparisons with other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo. Proteomic analysis of two specimens identified 18 endogenous proteins, and the Denisova-specific COL1A2-996 R>K mutation strongly supported their affiliation with the Denisovan lineage. Extended analysis identifies a set of shared morphological traits between Denisovan fossils (Xujiayao and Harbin) and other East Asian late Middle Pleistocene archaic Homo (such as Jinniushan, Dali and Hualongdong), indicating that they all belong to the Denisovan lineage. This analysis provides a comprehensive view of Denisovan features, showing both traits reminiscent of Homo erectus (such as a thick cranial vault) and those characteristic of modern humans (for example, a strongly arched temporal squama). They also share features with late Neanderthals, such as the structure of the temporal labyrinth and the presence of a suprainiac fossa. Notably, Denisovans are distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism.

papers.title: Beyond social bonding: Sex-specific regulation of familiarity-dependent mate choice by oxytocin in medaka.
papers.abstract: Oxytocin (OXT) contributes to social recognition and selective social behavior, but its effects depend on sex and behavioral context. Medaka (Oryzias latipes) reveal this dependence within a single species: wild-type females preferentially accept visually familiarized males, whereas wild-type males court females relatively independently of familiarity. Disruption of the oxt-oxtra pathway produces contrasting phenotypes. Mutant females show high receptivity even without visual familiarization, whereas mutant males show reduced courtship toward socially unfamiliar females and enhanced mate guarding toward familiar females. These findings distinguish recognizing familiarity from using it to guide mating behavior. A recent preprint reports similar behavioral and TN-GnRH3 circuit abnormalities in OXT-signaling-deficient and c1qb-mutant females, supporting a working model involving C1q-associated circuit refinement at an undetermined stage. How OXT signaling regulates microglial function remains unresolved, as does the circuit mechanism underlying the male phenotype. We propose that OXT calibrates the behavioral influence of familiarity within sex-specific mating circuits. This model accommodates female selectivity and broader male courtship without assigning OXT a uniformly affiliative function. Future studies will require separate assays of recognition and behavioral valuation, together with temporally and cell-type-restricted manipulations.

papers.title: Ultrasound in fetal growth restriction.
papers.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality. Its recognition requires differentiation from a constitutionally small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetus. Based on the current AWMF S2k guideline, this CME review summarizes the ultrasound assessment and clinical management of suspected FGR. Accurate first-trimester dating, standardized fetal biometry, assessment of amniotic fluid volume, and detailed anatomical evaluation form the basis of diagnosis. Consensus-based criteria distinguish early FGR before 32 + 0 weeks' gestation from late FGR at or beyond 32 + 0 weeks' gestation. Multivessel Doppler assessment of the umbilical artery, middle cerebral artery, cerebroplacental ratio, and ductus venosus provides complementary information on placental resistance, fetal redistribution, and cardiovascular decompensation. Cardiotocography, including computerized analysis of short-term variation in early FGR, is used as part of multimodal surveillance and should not be interpreted in isolation. The review discusses appropriate monitoring intervals, indications for inpatient care, antenatal corticosteroids and fetal neuroprotection when preterm birth is anticipated, as well as gestational-age- and finding-dependent timing and mode of delivery. A practical clinical case illustrates the diagnostic pathway from abnormal fetal biometry to delivery planning. Die fetale Wachstumsrestriktion (FGR) ist mit einer erhöhten perinatalen Morbidität und Mortalität assoziiert. Eine wesentliche diagnostische Herausforderung besteht in der Abgrenzung zu einem konstitutionell kleinen Feten (small for gestational age, SGA). Dieser CME-Beitrag fasst auf Grundlage der aktuellen AWMF-S2k-Leitlinie die sonografische Diagnostik und das klinische Management bei Verdacht auf eine fetale Wachstumsrestriktion zusammen. Grundlage der Diagnostik sind eine exakte Schwangerschaftsdatierung im ersten Trimenon, standardisiert

papers.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula.
papers.abstract: It has been unclear how Roman and later Germanic political control shaped the demography of Iberia and how it differed from other parts of Europe. We report genetic data from 243 ancient individuals dating to 100-800 CE, analyzed alongside 58 previously published individuals. In Roman times, we document an influx of people with ancestry from the Eastern Mediterranean and an influx of North Africans, especially in the center and south. Beginning in the 5th century, Germanic and Alan (Sarmatian) groups assumed political control. Although we identify individuals with Central-Northern European-associated ancestry, including siblings buried ∼725 km apart, the Hispano-Roman population remained continuous in Iberia. These demographic patterns contrast sharply with those in Britain, where major demographic change followed Rome's collapse, and with those in the central Mediterranean, where both periods were associated with profound transformations. Together, these findings highlight regional variation in admixture and continuity across post-Roman Europe.

papers.title: Mating preference evolution has sex-opposite effects on species persistence under reproductive interference.
papers.abstract: Reproductive interference, where interspecific mating activities have negative effects on reproductive output, can impact the expansion of one species' range into that of a related competitor. Theory to date suggests that if species recognition mechanisms evolve rapidly enough, the attenuation of reproductive interference may allow range expansions to proceed (a form of evolutionary rescue). Here, we show that sex differences cause evolvability not to have a uniformly positive effect on population fitness at the range front, nor on coexistence. We allow mate choice to evolve in males, where it takes the form of a courtship bias towards conspecific females, and/or in females, where a receptivity bias favours conspecific males. The beneficial effect of rapid evolution is highly contingent on 1) the asymmetry in the evolvability of mate preference between the two species and 2) the sex that controls the outcome of mating interactions. When female preferences dictate mating outcomes, rapid evolution increases the likelihood of range expansion by the fast evolving species, the other species being outcompeted. In contrast, rapid evolution of male mate choice has a detrimental effect on persistence in the zone of potential coexistence. We also show that if both sexes evolve their preferences, the female effect tends to override the male effect, and evolvability's net effect on population fitness remains positive. Thus, while rapid evolution of traits related to reproductive interference likely aid range expansion, case by case inference requires knowledge of the mating systems in question.

papers.title: Navigating normative terrain. Young trans women's narratives about gender, body and sexuality in Sweden.
papers.abstract: Despite growing research on transgender lives, adolescents' own perspectives remain less clearly understood. This qualitative study explored how young trans women experience sexual subjectivity in relation to embodiment, recognition, and gender-affirming hormone treatment. Eight semi-structured interviews were conducted with trans women aged 16-19 who initiated oestrogen treatment before or shortly after turning 18. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants evaluated their womanhood in relation to cisgender women's bodies and described fears of rejection and disclosure. Being desired by men could affirm femininity, whereas fear of rejection led some to avoid dating or sex, and genital dysphoria restricted sexual touch. Oestrogen-related bodily changes reduced dysphoria and increased bodily comfort. Sexual desire became less frequent and intrusive and, for some, more responsive to the presence of another person. Fertility decisions reflected whether genetic parenthood could be reconciled with identifying as a mother. Sexual well-being was linked to bodily comfort and recognition as a woman. Oestrogen reduced dysphoria and altered sexual desire but did not remove concerns about rejection, disclosure or stigma. Gender-affirming care should include conversations about sexual boundaries and disclosure, changes in desire and intimacy, partner relationships, and how fertility options relate to desired parental roles.

papers.title: The Event-Level Association Between Alcohol Use and Intimate Partner Violence Perpetration: A Systematic Narrative Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetration is a significant public health concern, with up to 90% of individuals in intimate relationships experiencing some form of physical, psychological, or sexual IPV from their partner throughout their lifetime. Over 30 years of research have concluded that alcohol use results in greater risk for IPV perpetration. Despite this known association, only recently has alcohol use been examined as a proximal predictor of IPV perpetration in daily diary-type studies. The present study aimed to provide a systematic narrative review of current research on the event-level association between alcohol use and psychological, physical, and sexual IPV perpetration. Relevant studies were obtained by searching PsycInfo, PubMed, and CINAHL. Full-text peer-reviewed studies published in English that quantitatively assessed the event-level association between alcohol use and physical, psychological, and/or sexual IPV perpetration (N = 24) were retained. Results provide support for the event-level association between alcohol use and IPV perpetration across college student, couple, community, clinical, and adjudicated samples. Future research is needed to distinguish whether certain patterns of alcohol use, quantity, or level of intoxication are associated with greater IPV risk. Similarly, future studies should aim to examine psychological, physical, and sexual IPV perpetration separately, and to identify how other known risk factors may interact with alcohol use to predict event-level IPV perpetration. These findings highlight the usefulness of clinical intervention efforts that provide skills to target urges to drink or to aggress in the moment when they are needed, with the ultimate goal of reducing alcohol-related IPV perpetration.

papers.title: Sex Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Responses to Adolescents' Questions on Romantic Relationships and Sexuality.
papers.abstract: Large language model chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have garnered increasing attention in the field of education, due to its versatility, processing speed, and widespread accessibility. However, its application to sexual education remains understudied, highlighting the need for more research into its potential to support informed decision-making among youth. The current study aimed to document ChatGPT-3.5 responses to adolescents' questions about romantic relationships and sexuality, using a more-than-human netnography approach. To obtain these responses, 393 anonymized emails written in French and English from adolescents aged 14 to 16 were collected from a recognized youth support organization. Data were obtained through ChatGPT-3.5 from January 14 to 31, 2024. The analyses focused on identifying content violations and describing the response formats, followed by a conventional content analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 recommendations. Overall, 17.8% of the emails were flagged as potentially violating ChatGPT-3.5's content policy. Responses were provided in two formats: (1) structured text or (2) continuous text that both included an introduction clarifying the question, normalizing the experience, and/or validating emotions; a list of recommendations; and a conclusion promoting support seeking, and/or a positive outlook. The recommendations aimed to encourage adolescents to embrace authenticity and personal agency, practice self-care and build self-confidence, engage in open communication, develop meaningful relationships, and seek support when needed. The findings highlight ChatGPT's potential to contribute to comprehensive sex education for adolescents seeking information.

papers.title: Integrative systematics reveal an unusual species of pedunculate ground beetles lacking fossorial legs from Late Cretaceous Kachin amber (Coleoptera: Carabidae: Scaritinae).
papers.abstract: CONTEXT: The subfamily Scaritinae (Coleoptera: Carabidae) is a speciose, cosmopolitan group of ground beetles characterised by a pedunculate body form and modified fossorial forelegs, adaptations associated with a burrowing lifestyle in soil or sandy substrates. The fossil record of Scaritinae is scarce and only one Mesozoic species has been described up to the present. AIMS: A new genus and species of scaritine ground beetles is described from Late Cretaceous amber in northern Myanmar. Its phylogenetic relationship with extant lineages of Scaritinae was investigated and divergence times among lineages of Scaritinae were estimated. Its palaeoecology is also discussed from the perspective of morphological adaptation. TAXON: A Late Cretaceous pedunculate ground beetle (Insecta: Coleoptera: Carabidae: Scaritinae), Cretoscarites burmanicus gen. et sp. nov., aligns well with extant Scaritinae, yet it lacks the fossorial legs typically seen in modern scaritines. METHODS: Its relationship with extant Scaritinae was investigated based on two datasets using maximum parsimony, Bayesian inference and maximum likelihood: (i) 55 morphological characters belonging to 16 taxa (representing 6 of the 7 tribes and 13 of the 20 subtribes of modern Scaritinae); and (ii) a combined morphological and molecular dataset for 16 taxa, comprising a partitioned alignment of 2772 bp from COI and 18S sequences of seven taxa, representing 5 tribes and 6 subtribes. Divergence times within Scaritinae were estimated in a Bayesian tip-dating framework based on both datasets under a relaxed clock. KEY RESULTS: Phylogenetic analyses using various approaches and datasets consistently placed Cretoscarites burmanicus within Scaritini. Among Scaritini, the nominal subtribe was recovered as the most likely closest relative of Cretoscarites burmanicus. Results indicate that Scaritinae originated in the Middle Jurassic (ca. 167-168 Mya) and the major lineages started to differentiate during the Cretaceous. Th

papers.title: MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 Signaling in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Genetic Susceptibility to Profibrotic Progression and Clinical Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disorder strongly mediated by genetic susceptibility and aberrant epithelial repair mechanisms. Among the identified genetic factors, the MUC5B promoter polymorphism rs35705950 represents the most significant and frequently replicated risk variant associated with both familial and sporadic IPF. This review focuses on the mechanistic role of MUC5B dysregulation in promoting epithelial dysfunction and profibrotic signalling, with particular emphasis on its interaction with transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signalling and KL-6-associated epithelial injury. Excessive MUC5B expression within distal airways disrupts mucociliary homeostasis, prolongs epithelial exposure to inhaled toxic stimuli, and enhances persistent alveolar stress, thereby facilitating chronic epithelial injury and aberrant tissue repair. Sustained epithelial damage subsequently activates TGF-β-mediated SMAD signalling pathways, promoting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and extracellular matrix deposition. Emerging evidence further suggests a close relationship between MUC5B-associated epithelial dysfunction and elevated KL-6 expression, indicating that KL-6 may function as a downstream biomarker indicating ongoing epithelial injury and fibrotic progression. The proposed MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 mechanistic signaling provides an integrated molecular network linking genetic susceptibility, epithelial dysfunction, biomarker elevation, and progressive fibrosis in IPF. In addition, telomere-related and surfactant-associated gene mutations further lead to epithelial instability and impaired regenerative capacity. Together, these interconnected molecular mechanisms provide significant insights into IPF progression and may support the development of biomarker-driven prognostic approaches and targeted precision therapies for improved disease management.

papers.title: Young adults' understanding of, and reaction to, those with uncertain genetic results.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Genetic advances increase the likelihood that children may receive uncertain diagnoses such as cystic fibrosis screen positive inconclusive diagnosis (CFSPID) from newborn screening. Research suggests a profound impact on parents. Research is needed to understand the impact on the child, especially at key developmental points such as young adulthood, when identity forms. As young adults (YA) are influenced by peer reactions, this novel study explored YAs' sensemaking of CFSPID, and their hypothetical reactions to peers or romantic partners with CFSPID. METHODS: Four focus groups were conducted and analysed using thematic analysis across three sections: understanding, peer and romantic relationships. RESULTS: Understanding: Without knowledge about CFSPID, participants used cystic fibrosis, genetic and contagious illness knowledge to form assumptions. Peer and romantic relationships: In both sections, YAs wanted to support their friend/partner; however, their responses revealed assumptions that a person with CFSPID would need more physical and psychological support and would be seen differently by some. Most wanted to learn more but were unsure whether it was appropriate to ask the person with CFPSID. Although rare, some reported they would avoid romantic relationships with YAs with CFSPID. All data suggesting people with CFPSID would be treated differently was based on erroneous assumptions due to a lack of CFSPID knowledge. Providing information about how CFPSID is different from CF did not appear sufficient to stop a reliance on CF knowledge when making sense of CFSPID. CONCLUSION: Further research should explore whether it's possible to change assumptions when YAs disclose uncertain results.

papers.title: Ion-pair complexes of oxidorhenate(V) with phenolate-oxazoline ligands: synthesis, solvatochromism and catalytic properties.
papers.abstract: Ion-pair complexes, in which an organic cation exists entirely in the second coordination sphere of an anionic metal complex, represent a structurally and electronically distinct compound class, whose solution behavior is influenced by solvent polarity and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Their capacity to undergo ion pair charge transfer (IPCT) transitions makes them attractive model complexes for ion-pairing equilibria and potential active species in catalytic cycles. Herein we report the synthesis, structural characterization, spectroscopic investigation and catalytic evaluation of the oxidorhenate(V) outer-sphere ion pair complexes (H2L1)[ReOCl3(L1)] (1) and (H2L2)[ReOCl3(L2)] (2). Both complexes crystallize as contact ion pairs stabilized by N-H⋯Cl and O-H⋯Cl hydrogen bonds. The hydrogen-bond-accepting Re-Cl bonds are significantly elongated as shown by single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, indicating enhanced lability at these sites. Both complexes display a striking solvatochromism, assigned by UV/Vis spectroscopy to an IPCT transition operative exclusively in apolar media (λmax = 555 nm, ε = 2700 L mol-1 cm-1 for 1; λmax = 577 nm, ε = 920 L mol-1 cm-1 for 2, solvent: CHCl3). Additionally, DFT calculations across a series of solvents establish the thermodynamic basis for the observed solvent-dependent ion-pair equilibria. Cyclic voltammetry reveals quasi-reversible Re(V/VI) couples for 1 in both solvents and for 2 in MeCN (E1/2 = +0.431 V for 1; +0.258 V for 2 in MeCN vs. Fc+/Fc). Both complexes catalyze perchlorate reduction with dimethyl sulfide, achieving 92% conversion (TOF 0.37 h-1) for 1 and 55% (TOF 0.22 h-1) for 2. 1H NMR monitoring shows that 1 is not converted into the bis-chelate complex during catalysis.
